_provenance: MEASURED STAGE-CONDITIONAL MOIC, PitchBook 'VC Returns by Series' Part IV (Q3 2024; US, n=31,642 companies taking a first VC round 2009-2018, measured 2024-06-06; COUNT basis; INCLUDES tracked failures - out-of-business plus no-major-round-in-6-years; gross, pre-fee; IPO payout marked at IPO PRE-MONEY). PROVENANCE OF THE NUMBERS THEMSELVES: PitchBook published the by-series MOIC figure as a chart and withheld its data labels - the PDF text layer for that figure carries only axis and legend text. Values were recovered by converting the page to SVG (pdftocairo -svg) and reading the 30 bar rectangles' geometry, then normalizing each series column to 100%. Precision +/-0.5pp. TWO INDEPENDENT VALIDATION LOCKS, both pass: (1) recovered seed <1x = 81.2% against PitchBook's own prose 'as much as 81% of seed investments return less than the original cost'; (2) mean(Series C, Series D+) = 49.5/40.9/6.1/2.1/0.9/0.5 rounds to 50/41/6/2/1/0, which are PitchBook's PRINTED Series C+ labels. Recovered by adversarial counter-agent, 2026-08-20. TAIL EXPONENT CONVENTION: 'alpha' is the SURVIVAL exponent P(>x) ~ x^-alpha; CSN density exponent = alpha+1. TAIL DETERMINACY WARNING: the survival exponent implied directly by the measured 20-50x and >50x buckets is seed 0.94, series_a 1.20, series_b 1.24, series_c 1.46, series_d_plus 0.76. An exponent <= 1 has NO FINITE MEAN - EV would be purely a function of where one caps. For seed (1.9%/1.4%) and series_d_plus (0.5%/0.5%) those two buckets sit at or near the +/-0.5pp recovery precision floor, so their tail ratio is NOT determined by the data; both are fitted under a constraint alpha >= 1.05 and their tails must be treated as indicative only. series_a, series_b and series_c have both tail buckets well clear of the precision floor and their exponents ARE determined. FUNCTIONAL-FORM LIMITATION: the lognormal-body + Pareto-tail form cannot represent the seed column well (16.2% max relative bucket error) - measured seed is a barbell, 81% dead plus a fat top, with a thin middle that a single lognormal body overfills. series_d_plus fits poorly for the precision reason above (23.6%). series_a/b/c fit within 10%. CORRECTED 2026-08-20 - WHAT THIS REPLACES: the vector previously installed as 'seed' (64.8/25.3/5.9/2.5/1.1/0.4) is NOT a seed distribution. It is Correlation Ventures' ALL-SECTOR, ALL-SERIES POOLED 2014 figure - reconstructed exactly as the n-weighted blend of CV's two published sector bars (Other VC n=19,412 at 65.7/24.6/5.8/2.5/1.1/0.4 and BioPharma n=2,228 at 57.0/31.6/7.1/2.8/1.3/0.3 -> 64.804/25.321/5.934/2.531/1.121/0.390). It is retained below as cv_pooled_2014_crosscheck, NOT as a stage. Likewise the previous series_b provenance cited a 'CV dollar-basis 37% <1x' that is CV's ALL-STAGES POOLED dollar-weighted figure, not a Series B figure; the constructed series_b (41.7% <1x) was 14pp OPTIMISTIC against measured B (55.4%). A REFUTED INFERENCE, logged: it was proposed that because CV's pooled <1x (64.8%) nearly equals CV's Series A <1x (65%), the pooled vector was 'Series-A-shaped'. REFUTED - the coincidence is arithmetic. Sweeping stage weights on a 5% grid over these measured columns, 133 distinct mixtures reproduce pooled <1x = 64.8%, spanning 19.7-26.5% at 1-5x and 4.2-8.2% at >=10x. One moment cannot identify six buckets. Measured Series A is 18.4% at 1-5x and 8.4% at >=10x against the pooled vector's 25.3% and 4.0% - importing the pooled mid-buckets would have HALVED the Series A tail. MEAN BASIS: do NOT target Correlation's 3.0X Series A average - it is DOLLAR-weighted while these bucket frequencies are COUNT-weighted. CV's matched count-basis pair is 65% <1x; its matched dollar-basis pair is 56% <1x with the 3.0X. For a per-deal analyzer the count basis is correct and 3.0X is the wrong object. UNRESOLVED, per the standing missing-inputs rule - ASK, do not average: Correlation's 2014 source is internally ambiguous about whether '2004-2013' is the FINANCING window (Booth's prose) or the EXIT window (CV's own chart subtitle). CV's later posts favour the exit reading. Affects only the cross-check vector, not the installed stages. Fee map unchanged: net = 1 + 0.8(g-1) for g>1, matches the audited EV trees.

seed._note: MEASURED. Tail exponent NOT determined at published precision (20-50x and >50x buckets are 1.9%/1.4%, near the +/-0.5pp floor); fitted under alpha>=1.05. Functional form underfits this column (16.2% max rel err) - measured seed is a barbell the lognormal body cannot hold. Gate tolerance widened to 25% with that documented reason.

series_a._note: MEASURED. Tail exponent determined (2.8%/1.4%, both clear of the precision floor; implied survival alpha 1.20). Best-supported anchor in this file. Max rel bucket err 8.5%.

series_b._note: MEASURED. Replaces a CONSTRUCTED vector that was 14pp optimistic on loss mass (41.7% vs measured 55.4%). Max rel bucket err 4.9%.

series_d_plus._note: MEASURED buckets, but tail exponent NOT determined (20-50x and >50x both 0.5%, at the precision floor). Fitted under alpha>=1.05; max rel bucket err 23.6%. Treat the tail as indicative only. Gate tolerance 30%: the 20-50x and >50x buckets are both 0.5%, i.e. AT the +/-0.5pp recovery precision floor, so their ratio carries no information and no functional form can fit them meaningfully.

cv_pooled_2014_crosscheck.what_it_is: Correlation Ventures, US venture financings, n=21,640, ALL SECTORS and ALL SERIES pooled (seed through late). Reconstructed exactly from CV's two published sector bars. Retained as an independent cross-check on the aggregate, NOT usable as a stage anchor. Was previously mislabeled 'seed' in this file.
cv_pooled_2014_crosscheck.window_ambiguity: 2004-2013 is either the financing window or the exit window; unresolved.
